title: Find a Peak Element
statement: A sensor logs a non-empty list of integer readings nums in which every pair of adjacent readings differs (nums[i] != nums[i+1] for all valid i). An index i is a spike if its reading is strictly greater than both of its neighbors, where any position outside the list counts as negative infinity — so the first or last element only has to beat its single in-bounds neighbor, and in a one-element list index 0 is always a spike. Every input is guaranteed to contain exactly one spike; return its index. Your solution must run in O(log n) time: binary search by comparing nums[mid] with nums[mid+1] and moving toward the rising side, since a spike must exist in that direction.
hints: The list isn't sorted, so what local comparison at mid still tells you which half must contain a spike?

If nums[mid] < nums[mid+1], the terrain is rising to the right, so a spike is guaranteed on that side; otherwise mid itself could be the spike, so keep it in the window with right = mid. Only compare mid to mid+1 — checking mid-1 needs bounds guards you don't need.

Use left, right = 0, len(nums)-1 and loop while left < right (not <=, or right = mid never shrinks a two-element window): mid = left + (right - left) // 2; if nums[mid] < nums[mid+1] set left = mid + 1, else set right = mid. When left == right, that index is the spike — return left.
